explanations.explanation: This neuron is essentially a Romanian‐language detector: it lights up on Romanian-specific tokens (e.g. the “.ro” TLD, words like „colaborare,” „pentru,” proper names in Romanian) and on Romanian orthographic cues (diacritics, common Romanian function words), marking stretches of text written in Romanian.

This neuron detects the very first, capitalized token of a web‐page title or section heading—e.g. article headlines, category/navigation menus or product listing titles—especially as used on Romanian sites.

This neuron fires whenever we’re at the very start of a Romanian‐language title, headline or section label—i.e. the initial capitalized bigram/trigram that kicks off article or menu headings (În-, Sc-, Even-, Ch-, To-, Com-, etc.).
This feature detects date‐ and time‐style tokens (years, day‐of‐month numbers and related uppercase timestamp headings), i.e. temporal expressions in the text.

This neuron detects the moment you hit a multi-syllabic derivational suffix at the end of a content word (–etc, –form, –id, –ens/–iuni, –iet, –ising, etc.), the kind of Latin-derived endings you see in Romanian (and occasional English) lists, specs and dictionary‐style entries.

This neuron is acting as a “current-context” tag detector – it lights up on the single token that names the page’s active section or filter (the date in a “last updated” banner, the city in a classifieds category, the chosen zodiac sign on a horoscope page, the book-title fragment on a literature site, the university name on an academic search, etc.). In other words, it flags the one token that carries the page’s dynamic breadcrumb or section label.
This feature is basically flagging “new‐word” subword tokens – it lights up on the very first subword (or whole word) at the start of each word, not on the continuation pieces.

Here’s a concise abstract description for each feature (shown by its most‐activated substring in **bold**):

1. **Ham**  
   Detects the “Ham” prefix in hotel chain names (e.g. “Hampton Inn & Suites…”).

2. **Bo**  
   Picks out the “Bo” prefix in hostel/hotel brand names (e.g. “Boogie Hostel…”).

3. **lan**  
   Fires on the “lan” prefix in product names for lanterns/lighting equipment.

4. **BC**  
   Marks the “BC” acronym that begins Romanian basketball club names (e.g. “BC SCM Timisoara”).

5. **E**  
   Flags an uppercase “E” at the start of a token—common in brand names and headings (“Epson…”, “EUR-Lex…”, “Etic…”, etc.).

6. **jo**  
   Captures the “jo” prefix in Romanian date/weekday expressions (“joi 10 ianuarie…”, etc.).

7. **Gab**  
   Identifies the “Gab” prefix of the personal name “Gabriela” in news items.

8. **cup**  
   Reacts to the “cup” prefix in Romanian words for cups/tournaments (“Cupa…”, “cupole…”, etc.).

9. **Ca**  
   Picks up the “Ca” prefix in Romanian financial or categorical terms (“Câștiguri salariale…”, “Categorie…”, etc.).

10. **roy**  
   Fires on the “roy” prefix in phrases like “royal romance actor,” i.e. the word “royal.”

This feature detects the very first, capitalized token of a section heading or post title—i.e. the initial word that marks the start of a forum thread, page section, announcement, or other prominent “title” line.

Here’s a compact description of what each feature has learned to pick out:

• Soft  
   Spots the token “Soft” (often capitalized) in Romanian contexts—almost always as part of software-related headings, product or company names (e.g. “Softul…”, “Soft parc auto”, “TotalSoft”).  

• Num  
   Fires on the Romanian “Număr” (“number”) label that introduces counts, inventory/statistical figures or report headings (“Număr de…”, “Numărul de…,” etc.).  

• Sort  
   Marks the “Sort”/“Sortare” UI label used to offer sorting options on lists or tables of products/data (e.g. “Sortarea produselor după…”).  

• Total  
   Picks up the “Total” part of the brand name “TotalSoft,” i.e. references to that Romanian software vendor.  

• Edit  
   Activates on “Editura” (“Publisher”) in bibliographic/catalog entries, flagging publisher names and related book-listing headings.
